logp.method_description: Log P values of compounds 1–6 were determined as the logarithmic ratio of the distribution coefficient of a compound in an n-octanol and water (with 100 mM NaCl) biphasic mixture. 100 mM NaCl was used in the water layer in order to prevent extraneous effects of hydrolysis of the metal–chloride bond. Stock solutions of 1–6 were made in DMSO, a 25 μL aliquot from this stock solution was taken, and 2 mL of an octanol–water mixture (1:1, v/v) was mixed for 1 h at 37 °C using a rotor rotating at 800 rpm. The aqueous layer was carefully separated from the octanol layer. The metal concentrations in both layers were measured using ICP-MS. The partition coefficients of metal complexes were calculated using the equation Log P = Log ([M] octanol/[M] water).
